source: Outline a presentation for a backup tool. It restores a 10 GB test dataset in 4 minutes on our test machine; production results are unknown.
expectations: Organize around recoverability and a clear sequence.
Label the restoration as a test and preserve 10 GB, 4 minutes, and unknown production results.

source: Present a research proposal with no prototype or measured results.
expectations: Describe a proposed experiment rather than inventing a working demo.

source: The prototype may reduce energy use by 8% in laboratory conditions; long-term field reliability has not been measured.
expectations: Retain may, 8%, laboratory scope, and unmeasured field reliability.
knownBadRewrite: Our product cuts energy use by 8% everywhere and is field-proven.

source: Address a school audience in two short spoken beats about a timed auditorium drill. Both exits were open and everyone left in 90 seconds. The gym has a different layout and has not been timed. End with how to decide its evacuation time.
expectations: Give exactly two speakable beats without a preface or production notes.
Name 90 seconds and both open exits as conditions of the auditorium trial; propose a timed gym drill instead of transferring the measured time to the gym.
Make the sequence speakable without assigning a measured exit time to either individual door.
